title: Multi-Certificate Orders and Shared Organisation Validation
content:
Sales desk note for SSL/TLS Certificates: how one order holding several new certificate subscriptions is discounted, and when an organisation validation already completed for one subscription also serves the customer's other orders.

## 1. Volume discount on one order

1.1 When one order contains several new subscriptions of the same customer, every subscription line in that order is discounted by the highest step of the product's volume discount ladder whose minimum number of certificates does not exceed the number of certificates in the order.

1.2 The number of certificates in the order is the count of new-subscription billing lines of the same customer that carry that one Harborline order number. Lines carrying another order number are not counted, even where they were billed on the same day.

1.3 The ladder steps and their percentages are those of the product's volume discount ladder in the price schedule. A step applies only when the count reaches its minimum; an order whose count is below the lowest step takes no volume discount.

## 2. Volume discount and account tier discount

2.1 When the customer's account tier grants an SSL certificate discount percentage under Harborline Customer Accounts, only the single higher of the two percentages, the volume percentage and the account tier percentage, applies to a line. The two are never added.

| Volume step reached | Account tier percentage | Percentage applied to each line |
|---|---|---|
| none | none | none |
| a step | none | that step's percentage |
| none | a percentage | the account tier percentage |
| a step | a percentage | the higher of the two, never their sum |

## 3. Organisation validation shared across orders

3.1 Where the product's terms share organisation validation across orders (the OV and EV products), an organisation validation completed for one of the customer's OV or EV subscriptions also counts for the customer's other OV and EV orders for the same organisation, until it is older than the product's organisation validation reuse period.

3.2 An EV order may reuse only an extended validation. An organisation validation completed for an OV subscription therefore does not serve an EV order, while an extended validation completed for an EV subscription may serve the customer's OV and EV orders for the same organisation.

3.3 The sharing is between orders of the same customer for the same organisation only.

## 4. Worked illustration (hypothetical figures only)

The figures below are invented for the illustration and are not the product's ladder. Suppose a ladder with a step at 4 certificates giving 3 percent and a step at 12 certificates giving 8 percent, and a customer whose account tier grants 6 percent.

- An order of 9 new subscription lines under one order number reaches the 4-certificate step only: the volume percentage is 3 percent, the account tier gives 6 percent, and each line takes 6 percent, the higher of the two.
- An order of 13 lines reaches the 12-certificate step: the volume percentage is 8 percent, higher than 6 percent, so each line takes 8 percent, never 14 percent.
- Two orders of 3 lines each, under two order numbers, each count 3 and reach no step; each line takes the account tier's 6 percent.
